name: CA-20
label: Safe R

key_factors: Fong's overwhelming fundraising edge ($2.4M vs $41K) and incumbency
Prediction markets price Republican win near 98%
No polls or expert ratings; challenger has minimal campaign resources
model.rationale: Every available signal points the same way: the district's R+16 lean, Vince Fong's incumbency and roughly 57-to-1 fundraising advantage, and market pricing near 98% Republican all overwhelm any factor favoring Sandra Van Scotter, whose campaign has raised little and has minimal cash on hand.
model.watch: A late wave of Democratic outside spending or an unexpected scandal involving Fong would be the most plausible forces to narrow the margin.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
California's 20th district leans heavily Republican, and incumbent Vince Fong enters the general election as a clear favorite. He has raised about $2.4 million and holds roughly $680,000 on hand, while Democrat Sandra Van Scotter has raised about $41,000 with under $7,000 available. No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, but prediction markets put Republican odds near 98 percent.

Fong advanced to the general election as the incumbent in a seat that has consistently favored Republicans by double digits. The district's partisan lean, his financial advantage, and the challenger's minimal campaign infrastructure leave Van Scotter with a narrow path. The main sources of uncertainty are the absence of polling and the possibility of late outside spending, but the structural picture points firmly toward Republican retention of the seat.
